title: Encode role-free context-boundary execution graph metadata
summary: Add canonical planning trace fields for work units, dependencies, waves, leases, route-backs, gates, context-boundary handoff, and publication serialization without role-based scheduling.

goal.outcome: Planning trace can carry role-free execution graph/context-boundary metadata that agency/runtime/graph surfaces use for safe parallel implementation handoff without spawning sessions automatically.
acceptance: Planning build schema or trace data supports work units, dependencies, waves, conflict scopes, lease plan, context-boundary reasons, expected outputs, required gates, route-back triggers, and publication serialization without a canonical role axis.
Agency planning reads or reports execution graph metadata as authorization context while preserving configured budgets and stop gates.
Runtime/status surfaces can project dispatch intent without bypassing leases, worktrees, fresh gate evaluation, or publication serialization.
Graph/read-model projection exposes execution graph/context-boundary metadata as a derived view only, not a second canonical graph.
TASK-specific tests cover execution graph parsing/projection, route-back/serialization metadata, context-boundary reason/expected-output shape, and no required role field.
non_goals: Do not spawn background sessions automatically in this metadata task.
Do not bypass artifact leases, gate reports, or publication serialization.
Do not create a second canonical graph outside planning trace data.
Do not make role a scheduling, policy, or gate criterion.
verification: targeted TASK-114 test for role-free planning execution graph metadata
targeted graph/lens or runtime handoff projection test
wiki_audit profiles=alignment,lexicon scoped to changed planning/runtime docs and tests

delta.desired: Planning trace carries canonical role-free execution graph and context-boundary metadata; runtime/graph project it for scheduling context.
delta.current: Planning output lacks consistent execution graph/context-boundary metadata and still references roles as if they could be scheduling fields.
delta.closure: Closed when planning builds can encode and expose context-boundary waves, dependencies, expected outputs, gates, and leases without executing sessions or requiring roles.
